summary.text: A 51-year-old woman with congenital dysplasia of both hip joints (Crowe type IV right hip dysplasia, right lower limb shortened by 4 cm, mixed contracture of the right hip) and latent iron deficiency anaemia was admitted for planned right hip arthroplasty with severe right hip pain, restricted movement and lameness. Concurrent conditions were arterial hypertension, chronic gastroduodenitis and chronic bronchitis in remission; she had an anaphylactic reaction to metoclopramide.

One year earlier she had a left total hip endoprosthesis (May 15, 2023); postoperative hemoglobin fell to 70 g/L and she was transfused with allogeneic blood, without iron levels having been determined or iron correction given.

On admission hemoglobin was 132 g/L with iron 6.8 mmol/L, transferrin 216 mg/dL and ferritin 92.8 mcg/L; ECG, echocardiogram, fluorography and leg vein ultrasound showed no pathologic change or thrombosis, and fibrogastroduodenoscopy found chronic superficial gastroduodenitis.

She received an intravenous ferric carboxymaltose infusion before surgery, then underwent right total hip replacement under general anesthesia on the 5th hospitalization day (110 min, blood loss 200 mL, tranexamic acid, cefazolin, autoreinfusion), followed by analgesics, nadroparin, omeprazole and rehabilitation.

No haemotransfusion was performed; hemoglobin was 97.5 g/L postoperatively, 86.0 g/L on postoperative day 3 and 84.9 g/L at discharge on hospitalization day 18. At postoperative days 28 and 90 rehabilitation was successful without infectious complications or other adverse events; a repeat ferric carboxymaltose 1,000 mg infusion was given and hemoglobin was 136 g/L at day 90 by self-examination.
